correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed exact domain and all index cases. For a three-value path beginning L_x>=3, inequalities imply 3/4<v/u<4/3; addition formulas and invariant ratio intervals prove the two index gaps equal. Lucas multiplication and signed remainders rule out even gaps and force b=L_k, odd x<odd k, and digits L_{k-x},L_x. The middle term of any four-value path is >=b but the exact triple classification would require it <b. For middle value 2 the unique prefix is 1->2->4 in base 2 and no next Lucas lies in [8,10). Odd k>=3 yield 1->L_k->L_{2k}, with last digit 2, proving sharpness. Exact verifier independently passed 8064 observed edges, 51 three-term paths, 561 family cases, and 3036 off-diagonal index-gap cases; these are consistency checks only, not substitutes for the full proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the canonical companion-sequence counterpart of an explicitly published Fibonacci right-digit-walk problem. A constant universal maximum independent of an arbitrarily large base, infinitely many attaining bases, and exact necessary-and-sufficient odd-index classification of every nontrivial three-value path are structural facts substantially stronger than finite single-base searches or a generic O(log b) termination theorem. The precise restriction to one-digit appending is intrinsic to the motivating walk definition.
